previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, chronic kidney disease, diastolic heart failure, and prior right knee replacement was admitted with worsening right knee pain, fever, and hypotension. She was found to have septic arthritis of the prosthetic knee, leading to septic shock and acute kidney injury. She underwent surgical removal of the infected prosthesis and placement of a temporary spacer. IV antibiotics were started and continued for six weeks. Her kidney function returned to baseline, and she improved clinically. She was discharged to an extended care facility for inpatient physical therapy and IV antibiotic administration, with plans for hardware revision in six weeks.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted on ___ and taken to the operating room 
by Dr. ___ the patient underwent removal of antib 
spacer, I+D and placement of new antibx spacer. The procedure 
was well tolerated and there were no complications. Please see 
the separately dictated operative report for details regarding 
the surgery. The
patient was subsequently transferred to the post-anesthesia care 
unit in stable condition and transferred to the floor later that 
day.  Overnight, the patient was placed on a PCA for pain 
control. IV antibiotics were continued as per ID 
recommendations. Lovenox was started the morning of postop day 1 
for DVT prophylaxis.

The drain was removed without incident. The patient was weaned 
off of the PCA onto oral pain medications. The Foley catheter 
was removed without incident. The surgical dressing was also 
removed, and the surgical incision was found to be clean, dry, 
and intact without erythema nor purulent drainage.

During the hospital course the patient was seen daily by 
physical therapy. Labs were checked both post-operatively and 
throughout the hospital course and repleted accordingly. The 
patient was tolerating regular diet and otherwise feeling well. 
Prior to discharge the patient was afebrile with stable vital 
signs. Hematocrit was stable and pain was adequately controlled 
on a PO regimen. The operative extremity was neurovascularly 
intact and the wound was benign. Infectious diseases recommended 
no antibiotics at discharge since her cultures were negative. 
The patient was discharged to a rehabilitation facility in a 
stable condition.

INDICATION:  Right knee pain, recent joint replacement failure secondary to
infection.

COMPARISON:  ___.

RIGHT KNEE, TWO VIEWS:  There is no significant interval change from the prior
examination.  Again demonstrated is methyl methacrylate within the joint
space, distal femur, and proximal tibia.  Soft tissue swelling is seen
diffusely about the knee.  Skin staples have been removed.  No areas of new
cortical destruction are present to suggest osteomyelitis.  There is no
fracture.

IMPRESSION:  No interval change in appearance of the knee without definite
evidence for osteomyelitis.

INDICATION:  Elevated white count.

COMPARISON:  ___ chest radiograph.

PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  The cardiac silhouette is within normal
limits.  As before, the thoracic aorta appears somewhat large and tortuous. 
Hilar contours are normal.  Pulmonary vascularity is normal.  The lungs are
clear.  No pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or areas of focal consolidation are
seen.  The osseous structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
